title: Man Charged With Murder After Woman Found Shot Dead at Hounslow Home
excerpt: Navneet Kaur, 26, was found with gunshot wounds during a welfare check on Chertsey Road. Rajat Jaswel, 31, faces murder and firearms charges and was due in court on Monday.
body:
• Navneet Kaur, 26, was found with gunshot wounds at a home on Chertsey Road in Hounslow, west London, on Wednesday, November 4, during a police welfare check, and was pronounced dead at the scene.
  • Rajat Jaswel, 31, of Chertsey Road, has been charged with murder and possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life, and was due to appear at Hendon Magistrates' Court on Monday, November 9.
  • Police say the investigation is continuing and have appealed for doorbell or dashcam footage from the area. Information can be given on 101, quoting reference 01/8264940/26.

A 31-year-old man has been charged with murder after a 26-year-old Indian-origin woman was found shot dead at a home in Hounslow, west London, the Metropolitan Police said on Monday.

Officers visited an address on Chertsey Road on the afternoon of Wednesday, November 4, to carry out a welfare check. Inside, they found Navneet Kaur with gunshot wounds. She was pronounced dead at the scene, having sustained fatal injuries, according to the Metropolitan Police statement.

The charges and the court appearance

Rajat Jaswel, 31, of Chertsey Road, Hounslow, was arrested shortly after Ms Kaur was found. He has since been charged with murder and with possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life, and was due to appear at Hendon Magistrates' Court on Monday, November 9. A charge is an allegation that will be tested in court; Mr Jaswel has not been convicted of any offence.

When officers first announced the arrest on November 5, the force said the arrested man had been taken to hospital for treatment, where he remained under observation, and that a post-mortem examination and formal identification would take place in due course. Ms Kaur's next of kin have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.

"Our thoughts remain with Navneet's family and loved ones as they continue to come to terms with this devastating loss."

— Detective Chief Inspector Sarah Lee, Metropolitan Police

Investigation continues, footage appeal issued

Detective Chief Inspector Sarah Lee, who is leading the investigation, said a man had been charged but the investigation remains ongoing, and detectives are still keen to hear from anyone who may have information that could assist — particularly doorbell or dashcam footage from the Chertsey Road area.

Anyone with information is asked to contact police on 101, quoting reference 01/8264940/26. Information can also be shared anonymously through the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 111 555, the number published in the Met's appeal.

What happens next

The case now moves into the court process, beginning with the magistrates' court appearance. Police have not released any further detail about the circumstances of the shooting, and the investigation remains open while officers gather footage and witness accounts from the area.

For the Indian and South Asian community in Hounslow and across west London, the killing has landed as a shock in a neighbourhood where many families have roots in Punjab and elsewhere in India. The police appeal is the one concrete step open to residents: anyone whose doorbell camera or dashcam covered Chertsey Road on November 4 can still contact investigators on 101 with the reference above.
